tools.change: WRONG FOR THE UK AS BUILT. The tool averages four frequencies (0.5, 1, 2, 4 kHz) and grades with the American six-step scale (normal to 25 dB, mild, moderate, moderately severe, severe, profound above 90). The British Society of Audiology averages FIVE frequencies (250, 500, 1000, 2000 and 4000 Hz) and has FOUR descriptors: mild 21 to 40, moderate 41 to 70, severe 71 to 95, profound in excess of 95 dB HL. Examples of what a UK clinician would be shown wrongly: 22 dB reads "within normal limits" (British: mild); 60 dB reads "moderately severe", a grade the British scale does not have; 92 dB reads "profound" (British: severe). The asymmetry flag (15 dB between the two averages) is also not the UK rule: NICE NG98 uses 15 dB or more at any 2 adjacent test frequencies. Change: a fifth field (250 Hz), the British descriptors, and the NICE asymmetry rule or no asymmetry flag. The audiologist role should see it too.

kitMechanismsMissing: A country cannot change WHO SEES a tool. The roles of each tool are written once in the shared English set (countries/_dil/en/araclar/arac1-3.ts); a country can only switch a tool off (kapali), rename units (birimAdlari) or change words (degisen). The UK needs, for example, the vertigo note for general practice and neurology too.

A country cannot ADD a tool of its own. The list of role tools (EN_ROL_ARACLARI) and the one base tool (EN_TEMEL_ARACLAR) are shared by all five English-speaking packs. NEWS2, the acuity record or the UK concussion stages would appear in the United States pack as well.

A country cannot give a tool its NUMBERS. The kit leaves thresholds and intervals to the pack (parametreler), but the English set builds every tool without them (araciBicimle returns no parametreler), so none of the eight "mechanism ready" slots can be switched on for one country.
Country numbers are not converted to the unit the arithmetic uses. A limit for haemoglobin supplied in g/L would be compared with a value the kit has already turned into g/dL (anemi-izlem).
HbA1c has no unit in the kit (lab-izlem accepts 3 to 20 only): a value in mmol/mol is refused. It needs to be a laboratory quantity with a unit, like creatinine.

Limits in the kit that the UK states differently and cannot override: the albuminuria categories (mg/g, not mg/mmol), the hearing-loss grades and the four frequencies, the 8.5 cm range of the expected height, the BI-RADS categories of the report outline, the stage list of return to sport, the ASA class list.

"Base" means every role, allied professions included. There is no way to say "every DOCTOR role": a core clinical tool given as base would also show to the physiotherapist, the dietitian and the audiologist.

The role list is one shared set of 40 keys (lib/ulke/rolEslemesi.test.ts refuses any other key). A country can rename a role but cannot add one (geriatric medicine), drop one (the second dermatology) or split one (oncology into medical and clinical).
The features "my templates" and "consultations" are not switched on in any English-speaking pack, so their two base tiles do not exist here.
